question: According to the unit, what is the key reason for introducing a transition signal on the very first day rather than waiting until later in the course?
options: Students are more energetic on day one and therefore respond better to new signals.
Day-one rehearsal makes the signal reliable by day five
Transition signals are only effective when students have not yet formed friendships with one another.
The first day is the only occasion when a teacher has enough spare time to explain and rehearse a new cue.
answer: Day-one rehearsal makes the signal reliable by day five
anchor: a signal that is introduced and practiced on day one becomes a reliable tool by day five

question: The unit argues that assigning small procedural roles to students from the very first day serves which purpose beyond simple task management?
options: It prevents stronger students from dominating whole-class discussions.
It gives the teacher time to complete the seating chart without interruption.
It builds a sense of shared ownership over the classroom environment.
It ensures that quieter students receive more individual attention from the teacher.
answer: It builds a sense of shared ownership over the classroom environment. — Assigning small tasks to students from the first day builds a sense of shared ownership over the classroom environment.
anchor: builds a sense of shared ownership over the classroom environment

question: When the unit describes the teacher's role shifting across the four-stage icebreaker sequence, which pairing correctly matches a phase to the teacher's role?
options: Pair work — discussion leader; whole-class phase — monitor.
Small-group work — audience; individual presentations — listener.
Pair work — monitor; individual presentations — audience.
Whole-class phase — monitor; small-group work — discussion leader.
answer: Pair work — monitor; individual presentations — audience. — During pair work the teacher acts as monitor, and during individual presentations the teacher acts as audience.

question: The unit states that positive feedback given to one student affects the rest of the class as well. Explain the mechanism by which this happens, as described in the unit.
answer: When the teacher acknowledges a correct answer from one student, every other student in the room registers that the classroom is a place where correct answers are acknowledged rather than taken for granted, making them progressively more willing to attempt answers themselves.
